rv.q: Jeezus! is a deliciously subversive, wholly irreverent, multi-layered musical that explores themes of Catholicism, colonialism and queerness.

Transferring from the Edinburgh Festival to the New Diorama Theatre, this very specifically 69-minute show (and it is too) is a bold, sacrilegious satire but with a big-hearted message about the true power of love.
The end result is fast-paced (69 minutes straight through), kitsch, ridiculous and often amusing.
Yes, JEEZUS! will shock and offend, and it sets out to do just that.

There are numerous characters within the piece and while Maggiolo skilfully maintains the central storyline, Lueches absolutely shines as every other character. There are some outstanding comedic moments when Lueches is playing Jesús’ American swimmer cousin, a part-time priest, part-time biology teacher, and even Jesus (the original one!) himself.
Though occasionally veering into sensory overload, JEEZUS! never loses its heart.
Alpaqa's musical is a reflective piece behind the laughs, with the message 'love is more powerful that God' coming through from the start.

cn.t: This irreverent, blasphemous musical about a Peruvian teen's sexual awakening with Christ wins critics over with razor-sharp humor, blistering performances, and bold queer defiance, though its sacrilegious content isn't for the easily offended.
